speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; please describe exactly where the pain is located and when you first noticed the rash. To help narrow this down, how many lesions do you have and have they appeared anywhere else on your body?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid_Factor, Anti_CCP
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_scan_of_rash

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; ESR: NORMAL READINGS; CRP: NORMAL READINGS; Rheumatoid_Factor: NORMAL READINGS; Anti_CCP: NORMAL READINGS; Dermatology_scan_of_rash: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies trauma to the wrist, reports a history of knee pain that resolved on its own. No other systemic symptoms mentioned. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That diagnosis of iron deficiency anemia doesn't explain your fever, active wrist pain, or the skin lesions; iron deficiency alone does not cause these acute inflammatory signs. Given your history of previous knee pain, have these joints become swollen or red, and does the wrist pain worsen with movement?

REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid_Factor, Anti_CCP, HLA-B27
REQUEST IMAGES: Xray_Wrist, Xray_Knee

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ESR: NORMAL READINGS; CRP: NORMAL READINGS; Rheumatoid_Factor: NORMAL READINGS; Anti_CCP: NORMAL READINGS; HLA-B27: NORMAL READINGS; Xray_Wrist: NORMAL READINGS; Xray_Knee: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Seronegative Spondyloarthropathy (likely Reactive Arthritis or Early Psoriatic Arthritis).

The normal inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) and negative autoimmune panel (RF, Anti-CCP, HLA-B27) effectively rule out Rheumatoid Arthritis, Sepsis, and Ankylosing Spondylitis. Given the triad of wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions without significant systemic inflammation, we must look for a localized infectious trigger or a specific spondyloarthropathy variant.

REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture, Synovial_Fluid_Analysis, Stool_Culture
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_close_up_of_skin_lesions
